description: Anomaly rule (#49) replacing the static 50% floor as the PRIMARY grade-quality detector. Seasonal decomposition (daily) z-scores the volume of correct math+reality decisions (gradebook.decisions.graded, filtered gen_ai.evaluation.score.label='correct' AND augmentloop.grade.source IN ('math','reality')) against its own recent history, catching a quality regression even when the baseline correct-rate itself drifts with the model roster (lifetime baseline ~58.8%, not fixed at 50%). DESIGN NOTE 1 (single query, not a ratio): SigNoz anomaly rules seasonally-decompose ONE query-builder series (confirmed against the platform's own canonical anomaly-rule example, ee/query-service/rules/anomaly.go + pkg/apiserver/signozapiserver/ruler_examples.go 'metric_anomaly' - a single builder_query, never a two-query formula). We anomaly-detect the COUNT of correct decisions rather than the correct-RATE ratio the static rule used; assuming decision throughput doesn't collapse in lockstep, a drop in the correct-count series is the same failure signature a rate drop would show, expressed the way this rule type actually supports. DESIGN NOTE 2 (evalWindow=1h, not 24h): the platform's own canonical anomaly example uses evalWindow=24h/frequency=3h, but empirically verified against this deployment's live data (2026-07-25, gradebook.decisions.graded, timeAggregation=increase): increase()/rate() return real values for windows up to ~3h and silently return null (no error) for windows of 6h+ regardless of groupBy or request type. evalWindow is kept at 1h (frequency 1m, confirmed inside the working range) to guarantee the underlying query actually returns data every cycle - a real, deployment-verified gotcha, not a stylistic choice. DESIGN NOTE 3 (seasonality=daily, z=3): 'daily' is the pragmatic middle choice given only ~1 week of hackathon-era history exists (weekly seasonality needs multiple weeks of baseline to mean anything; hourly is likely too tight for the current low, bursty event volume). z_score_threshold=3 sits mid-range of the requested 2.0-4.0 band. HONESTY CAVEAT: with only a few days of sparse, bursty (manually-triggered replay) history, the seasonal baseline this rule computes is thin - it will get more meaningful as real usage accumulates; it is not claimed to be well-calibrated yet, only wired up and verifiably evaluating.

annotations.description: Correct-decision volume (math+reality) is anomalously low (z-score {{$value}}, threshold {{$threshold}}) relative to its recent seasonal baseline.
